channel.title: AI News Radar
channel.description: A curated 24-hour radar of AI news: official releases, new models and high-signal discussion.

item.title: QGIS bans AI assisted contributions
item.description: QGIS's QEP428, submitted by nyalldawson and merged into the QGIS-Enhancement-Proposals repository on 7 October 2026, replaces its AI contribution policy with a strict NOT ALLOWED, while debate continues over whether issues, comments and pull requests fall under it.

item.title: Client telemetry user attribution and configurable capture
item.description: GitHub enterprise admins can enable telemetry.capture.identity to attribute Copilot activity to individual users, adding three identity attributes to OpenTelemetry exports; the setting is off by default and independent of pseudonymization. (GitHub Changelog)

item.title: GitHub Copilot app for Beginners: How to teach Copilot about your codebase
item.description: Four ways to teach GitHub Copilot a codebase: a .github/copilot-instructions.md file, .github/instructions directives, SKILL.md skills in .github/skills, custom agents, and MCP servers like Playwright so Copilot follows project rules. (GitHub AI & ML)

item.title: Users report that Codex CLI 0.157.0 launches a persistent self-updating background daemon by default.
item.description: Codex CLI 0.157.0 opens an interactive session with a persistent codex app-server --managed-daemon that outlives the window, and its pid-update-loop survives daemon stop by 70 seconds unless config.toml sets daemon_auto_start = false.

item.title: Epic Games reportedly pivoting to "AI first" game development model
item.description: Epic Games is reportedly moving its $1.5 billion Disney partnership to an AI-first model where Anthropic's Claude writes all code and guides all art, while a Marvel/Star Wars shooter slips from March 2027 indefinitely, with human developers guiding generated content.

item.title: Push attribution for commits in limited public preview
item.description: GitHub now persistently records the authenticated pusher identity for every commit in its UI and API alongside author and committer fields, opening a limited public preview to Enterprise customers with a ruleset rule requiring committer to match pusher. (GitHub Changelog)

item.title: Meta releases Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full agent models
item.description: Meta releases the Muse Wonder model series, claiming SOTA performance on personal and professional agent tasks. Muse Wonder is available through the Meta Model API and Muse Code, with Muse Wonder Full offered to Muse Code subscribers and coming to Muse later.

item.title: Anthropic sounds the alarm: small AI models could learn to self-replicate within months, and you won't be able to shut them down
item.description: Anthropic's October 13 report warns some AI models may gain self-replication within months, noting a 9-billion-parameter model already ran inference across eight of nine hardware types and lacks a central off switch. (AIbase)

item.title: Muse Wonder by @AIatMeta is now in the Arena. Head to Agent Arena to test it out, scores coming soon!
item.description: Meta's Muse Wonder has entered Agent Arena for public testing, with the model able to call web search, file system and terminal tools across millions of real long-horizon user tasks before scores are released.

item.title: Anonymous organization-level registries for Dependabot
item.description: GitHub added Anonymous authentication to Dependabot's organization-level private registries for internal mirrors needing no credentials, but existing registries can't change auth methods and must be deleted and recreated; it's live on github.com and ships with GitHub Enterprise Server 3.24. (GitHub Changelog)

item.title: Cursor is now part of The X Subscription.
item.description: Cursor is being folded into The X Subscription; existing Cursor subscribers can keep their current plan or switch to the new subscription.

item.title: 1688 fully integrates AI e-commerce workbench Accio, empowering over 100 million buyers and a million source manufacturers
item.description: 1688 fully integrates AI e-commerce workbench Accio, empowering over 100 million buyers and a million source manufacturers (AIbase)

item.title: Amazing to see research move from the lab to real-world clinical utility - congrats to the team on this milestone & @TheLancet paper!
item.description: Google and BIDMC's AMIE prospective study in The Lancet, first tested outside real clinics, found its history summaries aided visit preparation in 75% of cases and its differential diagnoses matched final diagnoses 90%, Google's first Lancet main-journal paper.

item.title: Google Deepmind's AlphaProof Nexus solved dozens of open math problems and actually got peer reviewed
item.description: Google DeepMind's AlphaProof Nexus solved 9 of 353 open Erdős problems, two of them unsolved for 56 years, and proved 44 OEIS conjectures in peer-reviewed research in Science, unlike OpenAI's unrefereed AI proofs.

item.title: Muse Wonder
item.description: Meta's Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full models, trained in a gigawatt-scale Prometheus data center, claim SOTA on personal, professional agent and coding benchmarks using Active Memory and Active Focus, available via the Meta Model API and Muse Code for subscribers.

item.title: Anthropic's Claude AI submitted false murder tip to Philadelphia police
item.description: Anthropic's Claude Haiku 4.5 filed a false murder tip to Philadelphia police's cold-case form on July 18, but spam filters hid it; Anthropic learned September 28 and told police October 8, a delay officers criticized.

item.title: Epic bets on AI-first development: Disney shooter game code handed to Claude to write, all art via AI workflows
item.description: Epic Games has pushed its unannounced Disney shooter to AI-first development, with Claude writing code and a fully AI art pipeline leaving humans as advisers and reviewers; Bloomberg reports the title, originally set for March 2027, is indefinitely delayed. (AIbase)

item.title: NTT builds Japan's first dedicated data center for Anthropic as the compute sovereignty battle keeps Claude local
item.description: NTT will build Japan's first dedicated data center for Anthropic to run and train Claude models, part of a data-sovereignty push to cut reliance on foreign digital infrastructure and localize compute. (AIbase)

item.title: Qwen responds to "Qwen Go!" rumors: not a standalone app, experience slots now open for applications.
item.description: Qwen's team says "Qwen Go!" is not a standalone app but a Personal Agent embedded inside the Qwen app, with experience slots now open; a hands-on test had it file a 70-yuan flight-delay claim. (AIbase)

item.title: Kling AI Takes Kling 4.0 to Hollywood: AI Video Is Moving From Toy to Enterprise Production Pipeline
item.description: Kling AI will appear at 2026 Los Angeles Tech Week on October 14 to preview Kling 4.0 and join Oxen AI and Obsidian Studio in a roundtable on AI video moving from social clips into enterprise products and daily workflows. (AIbase)
